newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - International sales, top brands shape tobacco Q3.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - International sales, top brands shape tobacco Q3.

text.p: International sales - though more tepid than in recent quarters - will continue to pace tobacco companies in the third quarter, while full-price brands remain healthy both overseas and domestically.
Analysts see double-digit profit growth once again at industry leader Philip Morris Cos Inc, with smaller but healthy gains expected at rivals.

International unit sales at Philip Morris, which has about a 48-percent market share in the United States, should be up about 9 percent from the year-ago quarter, but will lag the second quarter's 12.4-percent gain.

Philip Morris's third-quarter profit should grow in the region of 18 percent. Salomon Brothers analyst Diana Temple is looking for $2.02 per share for the period, while Oppenheimer & Co analyst Roy Burry is more conservative at $2.00.
Philip Morris earned $1.71 in the 1995 third quarter. The First Call mean estimate sees $2.01.
Burry also noted that the number of outstanding shares is expected to decline to about 818 million from 823 million in the quarter, which will help the per-share net.
Full-priced, premium brands will show strength for all U.S. cigarette companies, Temple said. She predicted a median earnings increase of about 14 percent for cigarette makers in the third quarter.
"It is encouraging that full-priced cigarettes continue to gain share, equaling about a 72-percent share up from 70 percent last year," Temple said, noting the figures are for the full year.
Also drawing encouragement this quarter is domestic sales, which have been on the decline for years.
"We're looking for good growth from the domestic cigarette market - better than usual," Burry said. "It looks as though the domestic market is flattening, no longer declining."

Domestic units sales in the period should have increased by about two to three percent for both Philip Morris and Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp, aided by "good price comparison and declining costs", according to Burry.
Domestic sales fell 0.4 percent in Philip Morris's 1996 second quarter. Year-ago comparisons were not immediately available.
A gain of anywhere between five to eight percent in international unit sales at RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp will be met with a decline of about four percent in domestic sales, the analysts said.
Both Burry's earnings view of $0.63 per share in the third quarter for RJR Nabisco and Temple's prediction of $0.64 lag the First Call market concensus of $0.67.
RJR Nabisco earned $0.61 per share a year ago, before a charge of five cents.
"The big question at RJR is Nabisco NA.A," Burry said. He said he expects an earnings increase of eight-percent for the separately traded, 80.5-percent owned Nabisco unit.
Philip Morris Cos Inc.......Oct 22......$2.01......$1.71
RJR Nabisco Hldgs Corp......Oct 22/23....0.67.......0.61
NOTE: U.S. company forecasts are provided by First Call.
